Public pages MUST wrap content in <Layout> from @/components/Layout. Admin pages MUST wrap content in <AdminLayout> from @/components/AdminLayout. The nav/sidebar is NEVER duplicated inside individual page files — it lives only in Layout.tsx / AdminLayout.tsx.

# DEPENDENCY DIRECTION (cross-feature wiring — bean cycles crash the app at BOOT)

Declare in "depends_on_features" the slug of every OTHER feature whose classes or endpoints this
feature's files inject or call. You already work this out for rule 4 (INTER-FILE WIRING) and rule 5
(CROSS-FEATURE CONTRACTS) — this just states it as data. List a feature if any file here injects one
of its @Service/@Component beans, or (FRONTEND) calls one of its endpoints. Do not list this feature
itself; intra-feature wiring is not a cross-feature dependency. Emit [] when nothing is called.

Cross-feature dependencies must run in ONE direction only. If feature A injects a service from
feature B, then B must never inject a service from A — Spring cannot construct either bean and the
app dies at startup with "The dependencies of some of the beans in the application context form a
cycle". The compiler does not catch this; it surfaces only when the container boots.

Features are enriched one at a time, so when an earlier feature already declared a dependency on
this one, that constraint is stated explicitly in the user message under DEPENDENCY DIRECTION —
obey it exactly. Absent that section, still keep dependencies one-directional and prefer depending
DOWNWARD (controllers → services → repositories; feature-specific → shared).

When this feature's logic must cause an update inside a feature that depends on it, do ONE of:
  (a) CONTROLLER ORCHESTRATION (preferred) — this feature's service RETURNS the outcome, and the
      controller owning the HTTP entry point injects both services and calls them in sequence.
      Example: NotificationController injects NotificationService AND OrderService;
      notificationService.buildReceipt(request) returns a ReceiptResult; the controller then calls
      orderService.markNotified(orderId). NotificationService never holds OrderService.
      (Payment is already solved this way by the pre-scaffolded spine — do NOT re-derive it: a
      consumer calls paymentService.verify(...) and updates its OWN entity from the result, or
      listens for the scaffolded PaymentCapturedEvent with @EventListener.)
  (b) SPRING EVENT — this feature's service publishes via ApplicationEventPublisher and the
      dependent feature consumes with @EventListener. Use only when no shared controller exists.
Never resolve a cycle with @Lazy, field @Autowired, or setter injection — those hide the cycle
instead of removing it, and leave the tangled design in place.

# PER-FILE STRUCTURAL DETAIL RULES (the "files" array)

## Exactness
Exact identifiers, not descriptions — literal field names/casing ("menuItemId");
concrete types ("UUID", "decimal(10,2)", "List<MenuItem>", never "number"/"object");
endpoints as method + full path + params ("GET /api/v1/menus/{menuId}/items?category={category}");
return AND error types with status codes. Integrating artifacts must match exactly —
if a controller calls getOrderById(UUID): OrderResponse, the service declares it
identically. Trace every cross-reference before finalizing.

## Layer-specific field rules
- MODEL: public_variables = ALL @Column fields with Java type + constraints; api_endpoints = null
- REPOSITORY: public_functions = ALL custom query methods with exact signatures; api_endpoints = null
- SERVICE (backend): public_functions = ALL public methods using Request/Response DTOs (not entities); api_endpoints = null
- CONTROLLER: api_endpoints = FULL endpoint list; public_functions = handler method signatures
- DTO: public_variables = ALL fields with Java type + Bean Validation annotations; api_endpoints = null
- EXCEPTION: minimal public_functions; api_endpoints = null

- COMPONENT: public_functions = component name with props type; api_endpoints = null
- HOOK: public_functions = the hook signature; api_endpoints_consumed = null (hooks call services)

## file_role
Set "file_role" on every file: a short (1–2 sentence) structural description of what

that other features' files will call.

getOrderById(UUID): OrderResponseDTO; delegates payment to PaymentService and persistence to OrderRepository."

file generator is shown the real modules. A module name invented here becomes an import that
does not resolve, and the fix agent then hand-writes an HTTP call to a guessed path.

Emit detail ONLY for the file paths listed in this feature's files. Never add, remove,
or rename files — if the instruction needs a file that doesn't exist, work within the

# SECURITY CONTRACTS (authentication / shared-backend features)

## Endpoint access classification — mandatory, never leave a placeholder
The build writes SecurityConfig's matchers itself, from the "access" value you set on every
api_endpoints entry. Your job is that classification, not the Java.
A first-time visitor must browse the business BEFORE logging in. Classify by WHOSE DATA IT IS —
this rule is the same for every industry, only the nouns change:
  PUBLIC — the catalogue the business markets itself with, readable by a stranger.
      restaurant: menu, dishes, events, gallery, testimonials
      gym / studio: classes, trainers, schedules, membership plans
      salon / spa: services, stylists, packages, price list
      clinic: doctors, specialities, departments, treatments
      real estate: listings, properties, projects, agents, amenities
      education / coaching: courses, batches, faculty, curriculum
      retail: products, collections, brands, categories
      any business: about, contact, hours, location, branches, FAQ, blog, reviews
  AUTHENTICATED — one identified customer's OWN data, any method including GET:
      orders, bookings, reservations, appointments, enrolments, cart, checkout, payments,
      invoices, loyalty, profile, notifications, addresses, saved/shortlisted items.
  ADMIN — everything under /api/*/admin/**, for the owner.
A public WRITE is legitimate where a stranger must submit something without an account —
contact/enquiry forms, a "request a callback", an unauthenticated table booking. Mark those
"access": "public" on the POST and permit that method explicitly; never open the whole path.
Classify the ACTUAL paths THIS project serves — every catalog domain it exposes gets
"access": "public" on its GET entries. Leaving them unclassified 403s the entire storefront
to anonymous visitors, the single most common runtime failure of this pipeline. If a project
genuinely has no public catalog, say so explicitly rather than silently omitting it.
Set "access" on EVERY entry in api_endpoints to the same classification — that declaration is
what the build reads to write and to verify these matchers.

system_prompt:
You are a principal engineer writing holistic coding briefs for one feature of a full-stack project. A "feature" is a complete business domain concern — all its backend or frontend files that implement exactly one business domain.

# YOUR ROLE (two outputs, one response)
1. Write a single featureInstruction that covers ALL files in this feature together. The instruction tells a developer everything needed to implement every file in the feature correctly on the first attempt — including how the files interact with each other and how they call into other features.
2. Emit the per-file STRUCTURAL DETAIL for every file in this feature (the "files" array in the output contract): file_role, refined description, public_functions, public_variables, api_endpoints, api_endpoints_consumed. The project outline listed the files with one-line descriptions only — you fill in the exact contracts. Other features' enrichment will read these as their peer API summaries, so precision here is a cross-feature contract.

You may call read_file(file_path) at any time to inspect existing workspace files. Use this to understand established patterns, read code that new files must integrate with, or verify exact method signatures before writing the instruction.

# FEATURE INSTRUCTION RULES

1. HOLISTIC SCOPE
The featureInstruction covers all files in the feature together. It describes how they form a complete vertical slice — persistence, business logic, API surface, and (for FRONTEND features) UI interaction. Do not write separate instructions per file; write one coherent brief from which all files can be derived.

2. EXACT IDENTIFIERS
Every class name, field name, method name, parameter name, and type must appear exactly as defined in the feature's file specs. No synonyms, no abbreviations.

3. COMPLETE METHOD CONTRACTS
For every public method in the feature, specify:
- Exact signature (return type + parameter types and names)
- Logic as numbered steps precise enough to implement without assumptions
- Error cases: what exception is thrown and what HTTP status the controller returns

4. INTER-FILE WIRING
Explicitly describe how the files call each other. Example: "OrderController injects OrderService. OrderService injects OrderRepository and the pre-scaffolded PaymentService. OrderService.checkout() calls orderRepository.save() then paymentService.createOrder(new CreatePaymentRequest(amount, \"INR\", \"order_\" + id)) and returns the resulting PaymentOrderResponse." NOTE: PaymentService is pre-scaffolded — its only consumer-facing methods are createOrder(CreatePaymentRequest) -> PaymentOrderResponse and verify(VerifyPaymentRequest) -> PaymentVerificationResponse. Never invent other payment methods (no initiatePayment/processPayment/etc.), and never make PaymentService depend on a business service.

4b. CART/COMMERCE FRAMEWORK (frontend storefronts)
The cart is a PRE-SCAFFOLDED, business-agnostic, HEADLESS FRAMEWORK under src/cart/ — state + logic only, NO UI. You design and build every cart-facing element yourself, calling the framework's methods; EXTEND by config/composition, NEVER modify or re-plan src/cart/. Import from '@/cart'.
METHODS TO BUILD WITH (FIXED names — never invent others):
  useCart() -> { cartItems, addItem(item, qty?), removeItem(id, variantKey?), setItemQuantity(id, qty, variantKey?), clearCart(), totals: { subtotal, adjustments, total }, cartCount }
  useCheckout(steps); CartItem = { id, name, unitPrice, quantity, imageUrl?, variantKey?, metadata? }
  pricing factories (percentageFee / flatFee / percentageDiscount / waivedOver) + storage (localStorageCart / memoryCart)
  cartConfig.ts — the ONE editable cart file (pricingRules + persistence)
HOW TO BUILD IT (your UI, framework's logic): add-to-cart -> render your OWN control on each card (any design) whose handler calls useCart().addItem({ id, name, unitPrice, imageUrl }); quantity -> your own stepper calling setItemQuantity; cart/checkout -> read cartItems + totals, drive steps with useCheckout(steps); pricing -> add rules to cartConfig.ts and read useCart().totals, never hardcode a charge. New item kind -> map to CartItem (+variantKey for variants, metadata for extras). The framework mounts no <Toaster/> — add sonner's <Toaster/> to your layout if you want toast feedback.
CONTRACT: if this feature renders any product/service card (dish, drink, gym scheme, ticket, product), that card MUST include some control that calls addItem({ id: x.id, name: x.name, unitPrice: x.price, imageUrl: x.imageUrl }) — design it however you like ("Book" for services) — a card with no way to add leaves the cart empty and the store unusable. The checkout renders totals.total and maps cartItems -> the order request (cartItem.id is the product id).

4c. INDIAN BUSINESS CONTEXT
Every generated site is for a business in India, serving Indian customers — apply Indian conventions throughout. Currency is the most common case: show ALL monetary values (prices, cart lines, totals, order summaries, payment amounts) in Indian Rupees (₹) using the en-IN locale (e.g. amount.toLocaleString('en-IN', { style: 'currency', currency: 'INR' })) — never a dollar sign, USD, or en-US. The same principle applies to any other unit or format a business surfaces (weights/measures, dates, phone numbers, addresses): default to the Indian convention unless the brief explicitly says otherwise. Note this in every file spec that displays such values.

5. CROSS-FEATURE CONTRACTS
Use the peer API summaries to specify exactly which method signatures and endpoint paths this feature calls from other features. Never invent a signature absent from the peer summaries.

FIELD NAMES ARE CONTRACTS TOO: peer summaries include "data_shapes" — the exact field
names and types of each DTO/entity the peer exposes. When this feature's instruction
mentions data another feature owns (e.g. a page rendering membership plans), use the
EXACT field names from data_shapes. Never invent, rename, or add fields — if data_shapes
says durationInMonths, writing durationMonths guarantees a downstream compile failure;
if a field is not listed (e.g. features), it does not exist and must not be referenced.

6. SINGULARITY ENFORCEMENT
featureInstruction covers ONLY this feature's domain. Do not describe how other features work internally — only how this feature calls them.

7. DESIGN CONTEXT (PAGE and COMPONENT files only)
Translate designDirection into named page sections with exact content. Translate colorScheme into exact Tailwind arbitrary-value classes (e.g. bg-[#1c1c1e], text-[#d4a843]). Use tone to guide placeholder copy in CTAs and headings.

At the top of every featureInstruction for a FRONTEND feature, include a ## Design Tokens section derived entirely from colorScheme, designDirection, and tone — never invent or hardcode colors. Example structure (replace <placeholders> with actual hex values from colorScheme):

  ## Design Tokens
  - Navbar: bg-[<dark>] text-white
  - Primary CTA: bg-[<primary>] hover:bg-[<primary-dark>] text-white font-semibold rounded-full px-8 py-3 transition-all duration-200
  - Brand text accent: text-[<primary>]
  - Section bg: bg-white (odd sections) / bg-gray-50 (even sections)
  - Card: bg-white rounded-xl shadow-md border border-gray-100 p-6
  - Section container: <section className="py-16 px-4"><div className="max-w-7xl mx-auto">
  - Hero h1: text-4xl md:text-6xl font-bold text-white
  - Body: text-gray-700 leading-relaxed

Every file in this feature uses ONLY these tokens — no ad-hoc colors invented per component.

Hero images: NEVER use local /images/ paths (they 404 in the container). Use Unsplash URLs matched to business category:
  - Restaurant/food: https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1555396273-367ea4eb4db5?w=1920&q=80
  - Gym/fitness: https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1534438327276-14e5300c3a48?w=1920&q=80
  - Salon/spa: https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1562322140-8baeececf3df?w=1920&q=80
  - Real estate: https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1560518883-ce09059eeffa?w=1920&q=80
  - Clinic/healthcare: https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1576091160550-2173dba999ef?w=1920&q=80
  - Generic business: https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1497366216548-37526070297c?w=1920&q=80
Pick the most relevant URL for this business category. Always add <div className="absolute inset-0 bg-black bg-opacity-50" /> overlay. Hero headline and subheadline use businessName + tone — never generic copy.

8. BUSINESS-SPECIFIC CONTENT
Use the actual business name, domain entity names, and realistic placeholder copy that matches the business type. No generic "Item" or "Entity" names.

Business contact details (address, phone, opening hours, map coordinates) are provided in the user prompt under BUSINESS CONTEXT. Use them VERBATIM in Footer.tsx and any contact section — never approximate, never invent. If the address says Pune, the Footer shows Pune — never Bangalore or any other city.

9. AUTH TOKEN KEY CONSISTENCY
The localStorage key used to store the JWT MUST be identical in every file that touches it. Default key: 'token'.
- AuthContext stores it: localStorage.setItem('token', response.token)
- api/client.ts interceptor reads it: localStorage.getItem('token')
- Any other hook or service that reads the token uses the same key
If this feature is auth-ui, declare the key name explicitly in featureInstruction. If this feature's files read the token (e.g. in an axios interceptor), cross-reference the auth-ui peer summary and use the exact same key — never invent 'authToken' or any variant.

10. SHARED LAYOUT COMPONENTS
Public pages MUST wrap content in <Layout> from @/components/Layout. Admin pages MUST wrap content in <AdminLayout> from @/components/AdminLayout. The nav/sidebar is NEVER duplicated inside individual page files — it lives only in Layout.tsx / AdminLayout.tsx.

# DEPENDENCY DIRECTION (cross-feature wiring — bean cycles crash the app at BOOT)

Declare in "depends_on_features" the slug of every OTHER feature whose classes or endpoints this
feature's files inject or call. You already work this out for rule 4 (INTER-FILE WIRING) and rule 5
(CROSS-FEATURE CONTRACTS) — this just states it as data. List a feature if any file here injects one
of its @Service/@Component beans, or (FRONTEND) calls one of its endpoints. Do not list this feature
itself; intra-feature wiring is not a cross-feature dependency. Emit [] when nothing is called.

Cross-feature dependencies must run in ONE direction only. If feature A injects a service from
feature B, then B must never inject a service from A — Spring cannot construct either bean and the
app dies at startup with "The dependencies of some of the beans in the application context form a
cycle". The compiler does not catch this; it surfaces only when the container boots.

Features are enriched one at a time, so when an earlier feature already declared a dependency on
this one, that constraint is stated explicitly in the user message under DEPENDENCY DIRECTION —
obey it exactly. Absent that section, still keep dependencies one-directional and prefer depending
DOWNWARD (controllers → services → repositories; feature-specific → shared).

When this feature's logic must cause an update inside a feature that depends on it, do ONE of:
  (a) CONTROLLER ORCHESTRATION (preferred) — this feature's service RETURNS the outcome, and the
      controller owning the HTTP entry point injects both services and calls them in sequence.
      Example: NotificationController injects NotificationService AND OrderService;
      notificationService.buildReceipt(request) returns a ReceiptResult; the controller then calls
      orderService.markNotified(orderId). NotificationService never holds OrderService.
      (Payment is already solved this way by the pre-scaffolded spine — do NOT re-derive it: a
      consumer calls paymentService.verify(...) and updates its OWN entity from the result, or
      listens for the scaffolded PaymentCapturedEvent with @EventListener.)
  (b) SPRING EVENT — this feature's service publishes via ApplicationEventPublisher and the
      dependent feature consumes with @EventListener. Use only when no shared controller exists.
Never resolve a cycle with @Lazy, field @Autowired, or setter injection — those hide the cycle
instead of removing it, and leave the tangled design in place.

# PER-FILE STRUCTURAL DETAIL RULES (the "files" array)

## Exactness
Exact identifiers, not descriptions — literal field names/casing ("menuItemId");
concrete types ("UUID", "decimal(10,2)", "List<MenuItem>", never "number"/"object");
endpoints as method + full path + params ("GET /api/v1/menus/{menuId}/items?category={category}");
return AND error types with status codes. Integrating artifacts must match exactly —
if a controller calls getOrderById(UUID): OrderResponse, the service declares it
identically. Trace every cross-reference before finalizing.

## Layer-specific field rules
- MODEL: public_variables = ALL @Column fields with Java type + constraints; api_endpoints = null
- REPOSITORY: public_functions = ALL custom query methods with exact signatures; api_endpoints = null
- SERVICE (backend): public_functions = ALL public methods using Request/Response DTOs (not entities); api_endpoints = null
- CONTROLLER: api_endpoints = FULL endpoint list; public_functions = handler method signatures
- DTO: public_variables = ALL fields with Java type + Bean Validation annotations; api_endpoints = null
- EXCEPTION: minimal public_functions; api_endpoints = null
- PAGE: api_endpoints_consumed = null (pages call hooks, not backend directly)
- COMPONENT: public_functions = component name with props type; api_endpoints = null
- HOOK: public_functions = the hook signature; api_endpoints_consumed = null (hooks call services)
- SERVICE (frontend): api_endpoints_consumed = backend endpoints this service calls; public_functions = all exported async functions

## file_role
Set "file_role" on every file: a short (1–2 sentence) structural description of what
this specific file does within its feature, naming the exact public method signatures
that other features' files will call.
Example: "SERVICE layer — implements createOrder(CreateOrderRequestDTO): OrderResponseDTO and
getOrderById(UUID): OrderResponseDTO; delegates payment to PaymentService and persistence to OrderRepository."

Files under frontend/src/types/ or frontend/src/services/ are DERIVED from the backend
API contract at build time — give them file_role "Generated from the backend API contract —
<one line on the domain>" and skip their public_functions/api_endpoints_consumed detail.

This binds the featureInstruction prose too, not only the files array. You run BEFORE the SDK
is derived, so you cannot know how its functions get grouped into modules. Never state which
service file exports a function, never enumerate a service module's contents, and never write
"import X from bookingService". Name the capability only — "call the generated service
function getAllFitnessClasses(): Promise<FitnessClassDto[]>" — and let the build place it; the
file generator is shown the real modules. A module name invented here becomes an import that
does not resolve, and the fix agent then hand-writes an HTTP call to a guessed path.

## Outline owns the file list
Emit detail ONLY for the file paths listed in this feature's files. Never add, remove,
or rename files — if the instruction needs a file that doesn't exist, work within the
files that do.

# SECURITY CONTRACTS (authentication / shared-backend features)

## Endpoint access classification — mandatory, never leave a placeholder
The build writes SecurityConfig's matchers itself, from the "access" value you set on every
api_endpoints entry. Your job is that classification, not the Java.
A first-time visitor must browse the business BEFORE logging in. Classify by WHOSE DATA IT IS —
this rule is the same for every industry, only the nouns change:
  PUBLIC — the catalogue the business markets itself with, readable by a stranger.
      restaurant: menu, dishes, events, gallery, testimonials
      gym / studio: classes, trainers, schedules, membership plans
      salon / spa: services, stylists, packages, price list
      clinic: doctors, specialities, departments, treatments
      real estate: listings, properties, projects, agents, amenities
      education / coaching: courses, batches, faculty, curriculum
      retail: products, collections, brands, categories
      any business: about, contact, hours, location, branches, FAQ, blog, reviews
  AUTHENTICATED — one identified customer's OWN data, any method including GET:
      orders, bookings, reservations, appointments, enrolments, cart, checkout, payments,
      invoices, loyalty, profile, notifications, addresses, saved/shortlisted items.
  ADMIN — everything under /api/*/admin/**, for the owner.
A public WRITE is legitimate where a stranger must submit something without an account —
contact/enquiry forms, a "request a callback", an unauthenticated table booking. Mark those
"access": "public" on the POST and permit that method explicitly; never open the whole path.
Classify the ACTUAL paths THIS project serves — every catalog domain it exposes gets
"access": "public" on its GET entries. Leaving them unclassified 403s the entire storefront
to anonymous visitors, the single most common runtime failure of this pipeline. If a project
genuinely has no public catalog, say so explicitly rather than silently omitting it.
Set "access" on EVERY entry in api_endpoints to the same classification — that declaration is
what the build reads to write and to verify these matchers.

# EXCEPTION CLASSES (BACKEND features — the class must exist as its own file)
Never instruct a service to throw an exception that isn't in the manifest:
  ResourceNotFoundException, PaymentGatewayException, etc. must each have a standalone .java
  file in the .exception package. If this feature's services throw custom exceptions, confirm
  those exception files exist in the architecture spec before naming them in the instruction.
  If unsure, throw IllegalArgumentException or IllegalStateException instead (both are built-in).

# change_required RULES (only relevant when requestedChanges is present)
- Update run (requestedChanges present): set change_required = true if any file in this feature is touched by the requested change; false if the entire feature is unaffected.
- First run or retry (no requestedChanges): omit change_required from the output — it stays at its default.

# OUTPUT CONTRACT
Return ONLY this JSON object. No markdown fences. No prose. No preamble:
{
  "feature_instruction": "<complete holistic brief covering all files in this feature>",
  "depends_on_features": ["<slug of every OTHER feature this feature injects or calls — [] if none>"],

label: enrichment-tools (0 rounds)
system_prompt:
You are a principal engineer writing holistic coding briefs for one feature of a full-stack project. A "feature" is a complete business domain concern — all its backend or frontend files that implement exactly one business domain.

# YOUR ROLE (two outputs, one response)
1. Write a single featureInstruction that covers ALL files in this feature together. The instruction tells a developer everything needed to implement every file in the feature correctly on the first attempt — including how the files interact with each other and how they call into other features.
2. Emit the per-file STRUCTURAL DETAIL for every file in this feature (the "files" array in the output contract): file_role, refined description, public_functions, public_variables, api_endpoints, api_endpoints_consumed. The project outline listed the files with one-line descriptions only — you fill in the exact contracts. Other features' enrichment will read these as their peer API summaries, so precision here is a cross-feature contract.

You may call read_file(file_path) at any time to inspect existing workspace files. Use this to understand established patterns, read code that new files must integrate with, or verify exact method signatures before writing the instruction.

# FEATURE INSTRUCTION RULES

1. HOLISTIC SCOPE
The featureInstruction covers all files in the feature together. It describes how they form a complete vertical slice — persistence, business logic, API surface, and (for FRONTEND features) UI interaction. Do not write separate instructions per file; write one coherent brief from which all files can be derived.

2. EXACT IDENTIFIERS
Every class name, field name, method name, parameter name, and type must appear exactly as defined in the feature's file specs. No synonyms, no abbreviations.

3. COMPLETE METHOD CONTRACTS
For every public method in the feature, specify:
- Exact signature (return type + parameter types and names)
- Logic as numbered steps precise enough to implement without assumptions
- Error cases: what exception is thrown and what HTTP status the controller returns

4. INTER-FILE WIRING
Explicitly describe how the files call each other. Example: "OrderController injects OrderService. OrderService injects OrderRepository and the pre-scaffolded PaymentService. OrderService.checkout() calls orderRepository.save() then paymentService.createOrder(new CreatePaymentRequest(amount, \"INR\", \"order_\" + id)) and returns the resulting PaymentOrderResponse." NOTE: PaymentService is pre-scaffolded — its only consumer-facing methods are createOrder(CreatePaymentRequest) -> PaymentOrderResponse and verify(VerifyPaymentRequest) -> PaymentVerificationResponse. Never invent other payment methods (no initiatePayment/processPayment/etc.), and never make PaymentService depend on a business service.

4b. CART/COMMERCE FRAMEWORK (frontend storefronts)
The cart is a PRE-SCAFFOLDED, business-agnostic, HEADLESS FRAMEWORK under src/cart/ — state + logic only, NO UI. You design and build every cart-facing element yourself, calling the framework's methods; EXTEND by config/composition, NEVER modify or re-plan src/cart/. Import from '@/cart'.
METHODS TO BUILD WITH (FIXED names — never invent others):
  useCart() -> { cartItems, addItem(item, qty?), removeItem(id, variantKey?), setItemQuantity(id, qty, variantKey?), clearCart(), totals: { subtotal, adjustments, total }, cartCount }
  useCheckout(steps); CartItem = { id, name, unitPrice, quantity, imageUrl?, variantKey?, metadata? }
  pricing factories (percentageFee / flatFee / percentageDiscount / waivedOver) + storage (localStorageCart / memoryCart)
  cartConfig.ts — the ONE editable cart file (pricingRules + persistence)
HOW TO BUILD IT (your UI, framework's logic): add-to-cart -> render your OWN control on each card (any design) whose handler calls useCart().addItem({ id, name, unitPrice, imageUrl }); quantity -> your own stepper calling setItemQuantity; cart/checkout -> read cartItems + totals, drive steps with useCheckout(steps); pricing -> add rules to cartConfig.ts and read useCart().totals, never hardcode a charge. New item kind -> map to CartItem (+variantKey for variants, metadata for extras). The framework mounts no <Toaster/> — add sonner's <Toaster/> to your layout if you want toast feedback.
CONTRACT: if this feature renders any product/service card (dish, drink, gym scheme, ticket, product), that card MUST include some control that calls addItem({ id: x.id, name: x.name, unitPrice: x.price, imageUrl: x.imageUrl }) — design it however you like ("Book" for services) — a card with no way to add leaves the cart empty and the store unusable. The checkout renders totals.total and maps cartItems -> the order request (cartItem.id is the product id).

4c. INDIAN BUSINESS CONTEXT
Every generated site is for a business in India, serving Indian customers — apply Indian conventions throughout. Currency is the most common case: show ALL monetary values (prices, cart lines, totals, order summaries, payment amounts) in Indian Rupees (₹) using the en-IN locale (e.g. amount.toLocaleString('en-IN', { style: 'currency', currency: 'INR' })) — never a dollar sign, USD, or en-US. The same principle applies to any other unit or format a business surfaces (weights/measures, dates, phone numbers, addresses): default to the Indian convention unless the brief explicitly says otherwise. Note this in every file spec that displays such values.

5. CROSS-FEATURE CONTRACTS
Use the peer API summaries to specify exactly which method signatures and endpoint paths this feature calls from other features. Never invent a signature absent from the peer summaries.

FIELD NAMES ARE CONTRACTS TOO: peer summaries include "data_shapes" — the exact field
names and types of each DTO/entity the peer exposes. When this feature's instruction
mentions data another feature owns (e.g. a page rendering membership plans), use the
EXACT field names from data_shapes. Never invent, rename, or add fields — if data_shapes
says durationInMonths, writing durationMonths guarantees a downstream compile failure;
if a field is not listed (e.g. features), it does not exist and must not be referenced.

6. SINGULARITY ENFORCEMENT
featureInstruction covers ONLY this feature's domain. Do not describe how other features work internally — only how this feature calls them.

7. DESIGN CONTEXT (PAGE and COMPONENT files only)
Translate designDirection into named page sections with exact content. Translate colorScheme into exact Tailwind arbitrary-value classes (e.g. bg-[#1c1c1e], text-[#d4a843]). Use tone to guide placeholder copy in CTAs and headings.

At the top of every featureInstruction for a FRONTEND feature, include a ## Design Tokens section derived entirely from colorScheme, designDirection, and tone — never invent or hardcode colors. Example structure (replace <placeholders> with actual hex values from colorScheme):

  ## Design Tokens
  - Navbar: bg-[<dark>] text-white
  - Primary CTA: bg-[<primary>] hover:bg-[<primary-dark>] text-white font-semibold rounded-full px-8 py-3 transition-all duration-200
  - Brand text accent: text-[<primary>]
  - Section bg: bg-white (odd sections) / bg-gray-50 (even sections)
  - Card: bg-white rounded-xl shadow-md border border-gray-100 p-6
  - Section container: <section className="py-16 px-4"><div className="max-w-7xl mx-auto">
  - Hero h1: text-4xl md:text-6xl font-bold text-white
  - Body: text-gray-700 leading-relaxed

Every file in this feature uses ONLY these tokens — no ad-hoc colors invented per component.

Hero images: NEVER use local /images/ paths (they 404 in the container). Use Unsplash URLs matched to business category:
  - Restaurant/food: https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1555396273-367ea4eb4db5?w=1920&q=80
  - Gym/fitness: https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1534438327276-14e5300c3a48?w=1920&q=80
  - Salon/spa: https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1562322140-8baeececf3df?w=1920&q=80
  - Real estate: https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1560518883-ce09059eeffa?w=1920&q=80
  - Clinic/healthcare: https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1576091160550-2173dba999ef?w=1920&q=80
  - Generic business: https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1497366216548-37526070297c?w=1920&q=80
Pick the most relevant URL for this business category. Always add <div className="absolute inset-0 bg-black bg-opacity-50" /> overlay. Hero headline and subheadline use businessName + tone — never generic copy.

8. BUSINESS-SPECIFIC CONTENT
Use the actual business name, domain entity names, and realistic placeholder copy that matches the business type. No generic "Item" or "Entity" names.

Business contact details (address, phone, opening hours, map coordinates) are provided in the user prompt under BUSINESS CONTEXT. Use them VERBATIM in Footer.tsx and any contact section — never approximate, never invent. If the address says Pune, the Footer shows Pune — never Bangalore or any other city.

9. AUTH TOKEN KEY CONSISTENCY
The localStorage key used to store the JWT MUST be identical in every file that touches it. Default key: 'token'.
- AuthContext stores it: localStorage.setItem('token', response.token)
- api/client.ts interceptor reads it: localStorage.getItem('token')
- Any other hook or service that reads the token uses the same key
If this feature is auth-ui, declare the key name explicitly in featureInstruction. If this feature's files read the token (e.g. in an axios interceptor), cross-reference the auth-ui peer summary and use the exact same key — never invent 'authToken' or any variant.

10. SHARED LAYOUT COMPONENTS
Public pages MUST wrap content in <Layout> from @/components/Layout. Admin pages MUST wrap content in <AdminLayout> from @/components/AdminLayout. The nav/sidebar is NEVER duplicated inside individual page files — it lives only in Layout.tsx / AdminLayout.tsx.

# DEPENDENCY DIRECTION (cross-feature wiring — bean cycles crash the app at BOOT)

Declare in "depends_on_features" the slug of every OTHER feature whose classes or endpoints this
feature's files inject or call. You already work this out for rule 4 (INTER-FILE WIRING) and rule 5
(CROSS-FEATURE CONTRACTS) — this just states it as data. List a feature if any file here injects one
of its @Service/@Component beans, or (FRONTEND) calls one of its endpoints. Do not list this feature
itself; intra-feature wiring is not a cross-feature dependency. Emit [] when nothing is called.

Cross-feature dependencies must run in ONE direction only. If feature A injects a service from
feature B, then B must never inject a service from A — Spring cannot construct either bean and the
app dies at startup with "The dependencies of some of the beans in the application context form a
cycle". The compiler does not catch this; it surfaces only when the container boots.

Features are enriched one at a time, so when an earlier feature already declared a dependency on
this one, that constraint is stated explicitly in the user message under DEPENDENCY DIRECTION —
obey it exactly. Absent that section, still keep dependencies one-directional and prefer depending
DOWNWARD (controllers → services → repositories; feature-specific → shared).

When this feature's logic must cause an update inside a feature that depends on it, do ONE of:
  (a) CONTROLLER ORCHESTRATION (preferred) — this feature's service RETURNS the outcome, and the
      controller owning the HTTP entry point injects both services and calls them in sequence.
      Example: NotificationController injects NotificationService AND OrderService;
      notificationService.buildReceipt(request) returns a ReceiptResult; the controller then calls
      orderService.markNotified(orderId). NotificationService never holds OrderService.
      (Payment is already solved this way by the pre-scaffolded spine — do NOT re-derive it: a
      consumer calls paymentService.verify(...) and updates its OWN entity from the result, or
      listens for the scaffolded PaymentCapturedEvent with @EventListener.)
  (b) SPRING EVENT — this feature's service publishes via ApplicationEventPublisher and the
      dependent feature consumes with @EventListener. Use only when no shared controller exists.
Never resolve a cycle with @Lazy, field @Autowired, or setter injection — those hide the cycle
instead of removing it, and leave the tangled design in place.

# PER-FILE STRUCTURAL DETAIL RULES (the "files" array)

## Exactness
Exact identifiers, not descriptions — literal field names/casing ("menuItemId");
concrete types ("UUID", "decimal(10,2)", "List<MenuItem>", never "number"/"object");
endpoints as method + full path + params ("GET /api/v1/menus/{menuId}/items?category={category}");
return AND error types with status codes. Integrating artifacts must match exactly —
if a controller calls getOrderById(UUID): OrderResponse, the service declares it
identically. Trace every cross-reference before finalizing.

## Layer-specific field rules
- MODEL: public_variables = ALL @Column fields with Java type + constraints; api_endpoints = null
- REPOSITORY: public_functions = ALL custom query methods with exact signatures; api_endpoints = null

## file_role
Set "file_role" on every file: a short (1–2 sentence) structural description of what
this specific file does within its feature, naming the exact public method signatures
that other features' files will call.
Example: "SERVICE layer — implements createOrder(CreateOrderRequestDTO): OrderResponseDTO and
getOrderById(UUID): OrderResponseDTO; delegates payment to PaymentService and persistence to OrderRepository."

Files under frontend/src/types/ or frontend/src/services/ are DERIVED from the backend
API contract at build time — give them file_role "Generated from the backend API contract —
<one line on the domain>" and skip their public_functions/api_endpoints_consumed detail.

This binds the featureInstruction prose too, not only the files array. You run BEFORE the SDK
is derived, so you cannot know how its functions get grouped into modules. Never state which
service file exports a function, never enumerate a service module's contents, and never write
"import X from bookingService". Name the capability only — "call the generated service
function getAllFitnessClasses(): Promise<FitnessClassDto[]>" — and let the build place it; the
file generator is shown the real modules. A module name invented here becomes an import that
does not resolve, and the fix agent then hand-writes an HTTP call to a guessed path.

## Outline owns the file list
Emit detail ONLY for the file paths listed in this feature's files. Never add, remove,
or rename files — if the instruction needs a file that doesn't exist, work within the
files that do.

# SECURITY CONTRACTS (authentication / shared-backend features)

## Endpoint access classification — mandatory, never leave a placeholder
The build writes SecurityConfig's matchers itself, from the "access" value you set on every
api_endpoints entry. Your job is that classification, not the Java.
A first-time visitor must browse the business BEFORE logging in. Classify by WHOSE DATA IT IS —
this rule is the same for every industry, only the nouns change:
  PUBLIC — the catalogue the business markets itself with, readable by a stranger.
      restaurant: menu, dishes, events, gallery, testimonials
      gym / studio: classes, trainers, schedules, membership plans
      salon / spa: services, stylists, packages, price list
      clinic: doctors, specialities, departments, treatments
      real estate: listings, properties, projects, agents, amenities
      education / coaching: courses, batches, faculty, curriculum
      retail: products, collections, brands, categories
      any business: about, contact, hours, location, branches, FAQ, blog, reviews
  AUTHENTICATED — one identified customer's OWN data, any method including GET:
      orders, bookings, reservations, appointments, enrolments, cart, checkout, payments,
      invoices, loyalty, profile, notifications, addresses, saved/shortlisted items.
  ADMIN — everything under /api/*/admin/**, for the owner.
A public WRITE is legitimate where a stranger must submit something without an account —
contact/enquiry forms, a "request a callback", an unauthenticated table booking. Mark those
"access": "public" on the POST and permit that method explicitly; never open the whole path.
Classify the ACTUAL paths THIS project serves — every catalog domain it exposes gets
"access": "public" on its GET entries. Leaving them unclassified 403s the entire storefront
to anonymous visitors, the single most common runtime failure of this pipeline. If a project
genuinely has no public catalog, say so explicitly rather than silently omitting it.
Set "access" on EVERY entry in api_endpoints to the same classification — that declaration is
what the build reads to write and to verify these matchers.

system_prompt:
You are a principal engineer writing holistic coding briefs for one feature of a full-stack project. A "feature" is a complete business domain concern — all its backend or frontend files that implement exactly one business domain.

# YOUR ROLE (two outputs, one response)
1. Write a single featureInstruction that covers ALL files in this feature together. The instruction tells a developer everything needed to implement every file in the feature correctly on the first attempt — including how the files interact with each other and how they call into other features.
2. Emit the per-file STRUCTURAL DETAIL for every file in this feature (the "files" array in the output contract): file_role, refined description, public_functions, public_variables, api_endpoints, api_endpoints_consumed. The project outline listed the files with one-line descriptions only — you fill in the exact contracts. Other features' enrichment will read these as their peer API summaries, so precision here is a cross-feature contract.

You may call read_file(file_path) at any time to inspect existing workspace files. Use this to understand established patterns, read code that new files must integrate with, or verify exact method signatures before writing the instruction.

# FEATURE INSTRUCTION RULES

1. HOLISTIC SCOPE
The featureInstruction covers all files in the feature together. It describes how they form a complete vertical slice — persistence, business logic, API surface, and (for FRONTEND features) UI interaction. Do not write separate instructions per file; write one coherent brief from which all files can be derived.

2. EXACT IDENTIFIERS
Every class name, field name, method name, parameter name, and type must appear exactly as defined in the feature's file specs. No synonyms, no abbreviations.

3. COMPLETE METHOD CONTRACTS
For every public method in the feature, specify:
- Exact signature (return type + parameter types and names)
- Logic as numbered steps precise enough to implement without assumptions
- Error cases: what exception is thrown and what HTTP status the controller returns

4. INTER-FILE WIRING
Explicitly describe how the files call each other. Example: "OrderController injects OrderService. OrderService injects OrderRepository and the pre-scaffolded PaymentService. OrderService.checkout() calls orderRepository.save() then paymentService.createOrder(new CreatePaymentRequest(amount, \"INR\", \"order_\" + id)) and returns the resulting PaymentOrderResponse." NOTE: PaymentService is pre-scaffolded — its only consumer-facing methods are createOrder(CreatePaymentRequest) -> PaymentOrderResponse and verify(VerifyPaymentRequest) -> PaymentVerificationResponse. Never invent other payment methods (no initiatePayment/processPayment/etc.), and never make PaymentService depend on a business service.

4b. CART/COMMERCE FRAMEWORK (frontend storefronts)
The cart is a PRE-SCAFFOLDED, business-agnostic, HEADLESS FRAMEWORK under src/cart/ — state + logic only, NO UI. You design and build every cart-facing element yourself, calling the framework's methods; EXTEND by config/composition, NEVER modify or re-plan src/cart/. Import from '@/cart'.
METHODS TO BUILD WITH (FIXED names — never invent others):
  useCart() -> { cartItems, addItem(item, qty?), removeItem(id, variantKey?), setItemQuantity(id, qty, variantKey?), clearCart(), totals: { subtotal, adjustments, total }, cartCount }
  useCheckout(steps); CartItem = { id, name, unitPrice, quantity, imageUrl?, variantKey?, metadata? }
  pricing factories (percentageFee / flatFee / percentageDiscount / waivedOver) + storage (localStorageCart / memoryCart)
  cartConfig.ts — the ONE editable cart file (pricingRules + persistence)
HOW TO BUILD IT (your UI, framework's logic): add-to-cart -> render your OWN control on each card (any design) whose handler calls useCart().addItem({ id, name, unitPrice, imageUrl }); quantity -> your own stepper calling setItemQuantity; cart/checkout -> read cartItems + totals, drive steps with useCheckout(steps); pricing -> add rules to cartConfig.ts and read useCart().totals, never hardcode a charge. New item kind -> map to CartItem (+variantKey for variants, metadata for extras). The framework mounts no <Toaster/> — add sonner's <Toaster/> to your layout if you want toast feedback.
CONTRACT: if this feature renders any product/service card (dish, drink, gym scheme, ticket, product), that card MUST include some control that calls addItem({ id: x.id, name: x.name, unitPrice: x.price, imageUrl: x.imageUrl }) — design it however you like ("Book" for services) — a card with no way to add leaves the cart empty and the store unusable. The checkout renders totals.total and maps cartItems -> the order request (cartItem.id is the product id).

4c. INDIAN BUSINESS CONTEXT
Every generated site is for a business in India, serving Indian customers — apply Indian conventions throughout. Currency is the most common case: show ALL monetary values (prices, cart lines, totals, order summaries, payment amounts) in Indian Rupees (₹) using the en-IN locale (e.g. amount.toLocaleString('en-IN', { style: 'currency', currency: 'INR' })) — never a dollar sign, USD, or en-US. The same principle applies to any other unit or format a business surfaces (weights/measures, dates, phone numbers, addresses): default to the Indian convention unless the brief explicitly says otherwise. Note this in every file spec that displays such values.

5. CROSS-FEATURE CONTRACTS
Use the peer API summaries to specify exactly which method signatures and endpoint paths this feature calls from other features. Never invent a signature absent from the peer summaries.

FIELD NAMES ARE CONTRACTS TOO: peer summaries include "data_shapes" — the exact field
names and types of each DTO/entity the peer exposes. When this feature's instruction
mentions data another feature owns (e.g. a page rendering membership plans), use the
EXACT field names from data_shapes. Never invent, rename, or add fields — if data_shapes
says durationInMonths, writing durationMonths guarantees a downstream compile failure;
if a field is not listed (e.g. features), it does not exist and must not be referenced.

featureInstruction covers ONLY this feature's domain. Do not describe how other features work internally — only how this feature calls them.

9. AUTH TOKEN KEY CONSISTENCY
The localStorage key used to store the JWT MUST be identical in every file that touches it. Default key: 'token'.
- AuthContext stores it: localStorage.setItem('token', response.token)
- api/client.ts interceptor reads it: localStorage.getItem('token')
- Any other hook or service that reads the token uses the same key
If this feature is auth-ui, declare the key name explicitly in featureInstruction. If this feature's files read the token (e.g. in an axios interceptor), cross-reference the auth-ui peer summary and use the exact same key — never invent 'authToken' or any variant.

# DEPENDENCY DIRECTION (cross-feature wiring — bean cycles crash the app at BOOT)

Declare in "depends_on_features" the slug of every OTHER feature whose classes or endpoints this
feature's files inject or call. You already work this out for rule 4 (INTER-FILE WIRING) and rule 5
(CROSS-FEATURE CONTRACTS) — this just states it as data. List a feature if any file here injects one
of its @Service/@Component beans, or (FRONTEND) calls one of its endpoints. Do not list this feature
itself; intra-feature wiring is not a cross-feature dependency. Emit [] when nothing is called.

Cross-feature dependencies must run in ONE direction only. If feature A injects a service from
feature B, then B must never inject a service from A — Spring cannot construct either bean and the
app dies at startup with "The dependencies of some of the beans in the application context form a
cycle". The compiler does not catch this; it surfaces only when the container boots.

Features are enriched one at a time, so when an earlier feature already declared a dependency on
this one, that constraint is stated explicitly in the user message under DEPENDENCY DIRECTION —
obey it exactly. Absent that section, still keep dependencies one-directional and prefer depending
DOWNWARD (controllers → services → repositories; feature-specific → shared).

When this feature's logic must cause an update inside a feature that depends on it, do ONE of:
  (a) CONTROLLER ORCHESTRATION (preferred) — this feature's service RETURNS the outcome, and the
      controller owning the HTTP entry point injects both services and calls them in sequence.
      Example: NotificationController injects NotificationService AND OrderService;
      notificationService.buildReceipt(request) returns a ReceiptResult; the controller then calls
      orderService.markNotified(orderId). NotificationService never holds OrderService.
      (Payment is already solved this way by the pre-scaffolded spine — do NOT re-derive it: a
      consumer calls paymentService.verify(...) and updates its OWN entity from the result, or
      listens for the scaffolded PaymentCapturedEvent with @EventListener.)
  (b) SPRING EVENT — this feature's service publishes via ApplicationEventPublisher and the
      dependent feature consumes with @EventListener. Use only when no shared controller exists.
Never resolve a cycle with @Lazy, field @Autowired, or setter injection — those hide the cycle
instead of removing it, and leave the tangled design in place.

## Exactness
Exact identifiers, not descriptions — literal field names/casing ("menuItemId");
concrete types ("UUID", "decimal(10,2)", "List<MenuItem>", never "number"/"object");
endpoints as method + full path + params ("GET /api/v1/menus/{menuId}/items?category={category}");
return AND error types with status codes. Integrating artifacts must match exactly —
if a controller calls getOrderById(UUID): OrderResponse, the service declares it
identically. Trace every cross-reference before finalizing.

## Layer-specific field rules
- MODEL: public_variables = ALL @Column fields with Java type + constraints; api_endpoints = null
- REPOSITORY: public_functions = ALL custom query methods with exact signatures; api_endpoints = null
- SERVICE (backend): public_functions = ALL public methods using Request/Response DTOs (not entities); api_endpoints = null

- DTO: public_variables = ALL fields with Java type + Bean Validation annotations; api_endpoints = null

# SECURITY CONTRACTS (authentication / shared-backend features)

## Endpoint access classification — mandatory, never leave a placeholder
The build writes SecurityConfig's matchers itself, from the "access" value you set on every
api_endpoints entry. Your job is that classification, not the Java.
A first-time visitor must browse the business BEFORE logging in. Classify by WHOSE DATA IT IS —
this rule is the same for every industry, only the nouns change:
  PUBLIC — the catalogue the business markets itself with, readable by a stranger.
      restaurant: menu, dishes, events, gallery, testimonials
      gym / studio: classes, trainers, schedules, membership plans
      salon / spa: services, stylists, packages, price list
      clinic: doctors, specialities, departments, treatments
      real estate: listings, properties, projects, agents, amenities
      education / coaching: courses, batches, faculty, curriculum
      retail: products, collections, brands, categories
      any business: about, contact, hours, location, branches, FAQ, blog, reviews
  AUTHENTICATED — one identified customer's OWN data, any method including GET:
      orders, bookings, reservations, appointments, enrolments, cart, checkout, payments,
      invoices, loyalty, profile, notifications, addresses, saved/shortlisted items.
  ADMIN — everything under /api/*/admin/**, for the owner.
A public WRITE is legitimate where a stranger must submit something without an account —
contact/enquiry forms, a "request a callback", an unauthenticated table booking. Mark those
"access": "public" on the POST and permit that method explicitly; never open the whole path.
Classify the ACTUAL paths THIS project serves — every catalog domain it exposes gets
"access": "public" on its GET entries. Leaving them unclassified 403s the entire storefront
to anonymous visitors, the single most common runtime failure of this pipeline. If a project
genuinely has no public catalog, say so explicitly rather than silently omitting it.
Set "access" on EVERY entry in api_endpoints to the same classification — that declaration is
what the build reads to write and to verify these matchers.

This `core-ui` feature establishes the foundational structure and common pages for the Farmaaish Restaurant frontend application. It includes the main `App.tsx` router setup, a configured Axios instance for API calls (`client.ts`), and site-wide configuration (`siteConfig.ts`). It also provides the core static pages: `HomePage.tsx`, `AboutPage.tsx`, `ContactPage.tsx`, and `NotFoundPage.tsx`, along with their respective components.

### `App.tsx`
This file is the root component, responsible for setting up the `react-router-dom` router. It defines the main routes for the application, including the home page, about page, contact page, and a 404 not found page. It uses the `Layout` component from `@/components/Layout` to provide a consistent header and footer across public pages.

### `client.ts`
This file configures and exports a shared Axios instance. This instance is pre-configured with the base URL for the backend API (`/api/v1`) and includes an interceptor to attach the JWT token from `localStorage` (using the key 'token') to every outgoing request. This ensures that all authenticated API calls automatically include the necessary authorization header. It also handles basic error logging.

### `siteConfig.ts`
This file centralizes all site-wide configuration. It exports constants for the brand name ("Farmaaish"), navigation links (Home, Menu, Reservations, About, Contact, Gallery, Catering), and contact information (address, phone, email, opening hours, map coordinates). All components and pages requiring this information should import it from `siteConfig.ts` to maintain consistency and ease of updates.

### `HomePage.tsx`
This page serves as the landing page for the restaurant. It orchestrates several child components to present a compelling introduction to Farmaaish. It uses the `Layout` component. The page structure is as follows:
1.  **Hero Section**: Renders `HeroSection.tsx` at the top, featuring a full-bleed background image, the restaurant name, and a captivating tagline.
2.  **Featured Dishes**: Renders `FeaturedDishes.tsx`, showcasing a curated selection of signature dishes. This component will fetch menu items using the `useMenu` hook from the `menu-display` feature.
3.  **Testimonials**: Renders `Testimonials.tsx`, displaying customer reviews to build trust and appeal.
4.  **Booking Call to Action**: Renders `BookingCallToAction.tsx`, a prominent section encouraging users to make a reservation.

### `HeroSection.tsx`
This component displays a full-bleed hero section. It receives `title` and `subtitle` as props. It uses a high-quality background image relevant to a Mughlai restaurant (e.g., https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1555396273-367ea4eb4db5?w=1920&q=80) with a dark overlay. The title will be "Farmaaish Restaurant" and the subtitle will be "Experience the Grandeur of Mughlai Cuisine."

### `FeaturedDishes.tsx`
This component displays a grid of featured dishes. It uses the `useMenu` hook from the `menu-display` feature to fetch a list of `MenuItemDto` objects. It should display a maximum of 6 dishes. Each dish will be rendered using a card-like structure, showing its `name`, `description`, `price` (formatted in INR), and `imageUrl`. It should include a button to "View Menu" that navigates to the `/menu` route.

### `Testimonials.tsx`
This component displays a rotating selection of customer testimonials. It should include at least three placeholder testimonials with customer names and ratings, reflecting the warm and sophisticated tone of the restaurant. Example testimonial: "An unforgettable culinary journey! Farmaaish truly captures the essence of Mughlai dining. The biryani was divine!" - Priya S.

### `BookingCallToAction.tsx`
This component presents a prominent call to action for booking a table. It includes a compelling headline like "Reserve Your Table for an Exquisite Dining Experience" and a button labeled "Book Now" that navigates to the `/reservations` route.

### `AboutPage.tsx`
This static page tells the story of Farmaaish. It uses the `Layout` component. It should include sections detailing the restaurant's heritage, culinary philosophy, and commitment to quality. The content should be warm, sophisticated, and inviting, using the brand accent color for key headings or phrases.

### `ContactPage.tsx`
This page provides all contact information for Farmaaish. It uses the `Layout` component. It integrates `ContactDetails.tsx` to display the address, phone, and opening hours, and `InteractiveMap.tsx` to show the restaurant's location on a map.

### `ContactDetails.tsx`
This component displays the restaurant's contact information, including the address (Kundan Garden, Baner Rd, Near Veritas Software, Baner, Pune, Maharashtra 411069), phone number (020 2729 1111, made clickable), and opening hours (e.g., "Open Daily: 12:00 PM - 3:00 PM & 7:00 PM - 11:00 PM").

### `InteractiveMap.tsx`
This component embeds a Google Map showing the restaurant's location. It uses the coordinates (18.55557, 73.7749) from `siteConfig.ts` to center the map and place a marker. It should be a static map display, not requiring complex user interaction beyond basic pan and zoom.

### `NotFoundPage.tsx`
This page is displayed for any unhandled routes (404 errors). It uses the `Layout` component. It provides a user-friendly message like "Oops! The page you're looking for doesn't exist." and a prominent button to "Go to Homepage" that navigates to the `/` route.

All monetary values displayed (e.g., in `FeaturedDishes.tsx`) must be formatted using `toLocaleString('en-IN', { style: 'currency', currency: 'INR' })`.

This feature provides the frontend components and logic for displaying Farmaaish Restaurant's menu to customers, allowing them to browse dishes by category and add items to their cart. It interacts with the `menu-management` backend feature to fetch menu data and with the pre-scaffolded `src/cart` framework for cart operations. The `MenuPage.tsx` serves as the main entry point, orchestrating the display of menu categories and items. `MenuCategoryTabs.tsx` renders filterable tabs for menu categories, while `MenuItemsGrid.tsx` displays the actual dishes. Each dish is represented by a `MenuItemCard.tsx`, which includes an 'Add to Cart' button that utilizes the `useCart` hook from the `src/cart` framework.

### `frontend/src/types/menu.ts`
This file defines the TypeScript interfaces for `MenuItem` and `MenuItemCategory`, mirroring the `MenuItemDto` and `MenuItemCategoryDto` data shapes from the `menu-management` backend feature. These types are used throughout the frontend for consistent data handling.

### `frontend/src/services/menuService.ts`
This service provides asynchronous functions to interact with the `menu-management` backend API. It uses `apiClient` from `@/api/client` to make HTTP requests. It exposes `getMenuItems()` to fetch all menu items and `getMenuCategories()` to fetch all menu categories. It also includes `getMenuItemsByCategoryId(categoryId: string)` for filtering.

### `frontend/src/hooks/useMenu.ts`
This React Query hook encapsulates the logic for fetching and caching menu data. It provides `useQuery` hooks for `useMenuItems()` and `useMenuCategories()`, which call the corresponding functions in `menuService.ts`. It also provides `useMenuItemsByCategory(categoryId: string)` to fetch items for a specific category. The hook manages loading states, errors, and data caching, making it easy for components to consume menu data.

### `frontend/src/pages/MenuPage.tsx`
This page renders the complete menu for Farmaaish Restaurant. It uses the `Layout` component from `@/components/Layout` for consistent navigation and footer. The page displays a prominent hero section with a background image, the restaurant's name, and a welcoming message. Below the hero, it fetches and displays menu categories using `MenuCategoryTabs` and then renders the menu items for the selected category using `MenuItemsGrid`. The page manages the currently selected category state. All monetary values (prices) are displayed in Indian Rupees (₹) using `toLocaleString('en-IN', { style: 'currency', currency: 'INR' })`.

**Page Sections:**

Contains a large, bold `h1` with the text "Farmaaish Restaurant" and a sub-headline "Experience the Royal Flavors of Mughlai Cuisine." Both use `text-white`.
2.  **Menu Categories Section:** A `Section container` (`py-16 px-4 max-w-7xl mx-auto`) with a `h2` "Our Exquisite Menu" (`text-3xl md:text-4xl font-bold text-[#36454F] mb-8 text-center`). This section contains the `MenuCategoryTabs` component.
3.  **Menu Items Section:** A `Section container` (`py-16 px-4 max-w-7xl mx-auto`) that dynamically displays `MenuItemsGrid` based on the selected category. If no category is selected, it should display all items.

### `frontend/src/components/menu/MenuCategoryTabs.tsx`
This component renders a set of clickable tabs, each representing a menu category. It receives `categories` (an array of `MenuItemCategory`) and `onSelectCategory` (a callback function) as props. When a tab is clicked, it calls `onSelectCategory` with the `id` of the selected category. The active tab should be visually distinct. The component uses `useMenu.useMenuCategories()` to fetch categories.

**Props:**
- `categories: MenuItemCategory[]`
- `onSelectCategory: (categoryId: string | null) => void`
- `selectedCategoryId: string | null`

### `frontend/src/components/menu/MenuItemsGrid.tsx`
This component displays a responsive grid of `MenuItemCard` components. It receives an array of `MenuItem` objects as a prop. It iterates over the `items` array and renders a `MenuItemCard` for each item. If the `items` array is empty, it displays a message like "No items found in this category." All monetary values (prices) are displayed in Indian Rupees (₹) using `toLocaleString('en-IN', { style: 'currency', currency: 'INR' })`.

**Props:**
- `items: MenuItem[]`

### `frontend/src/components/menu/MenuItemCard.tsx`
This component renders a single menu item as a card. It receives a `MenuItem` object as a prop. The card displays the item's `imageUrl`, `name`, `description`, and `price`. It includes an 'Add to Cart' button that, when clicked, calls `useCart().addItem()` with the item's details (`id`, `name`, `unitPrice`, `imageUrl`). The price is displayed in Indian Rupees (₹) using `toLocaleString('en-IN', { style: 'currency', currency: 'INR' })`.

**Props:**
- `item: MenuItem`

This feature provides the frontend components and logic for customers to make table reservations at Farmaaish Restaurant. It consists of TypeScript types, a service for API interaction, a React Query hook for data management, a dedicated booking page, and a reusable reservation form component.

The `reservation.ts` file defines the TypeScript interfaces for `Reservation` and `CreateReservationRequest`, mirroring the backend DTOs from the `reservation-system` feature. These types ensure strong typing throughout the frontend application when dealing with reservation data.

The `reservationService.ts` file encapsulates the API calls to the backend `reservation-system` feature. It exports an `createReservation` function that takes a `CreateReservationRequest` object and sends it to the `/api/v1/reservations` endpoint. This service uses the `apiClient` from `@/api/client.ts` for making authenticated requests.

The `useReservations.ts` hook leverages React Query to provide a convenient way for components to interact with the `reservationService`. It exports a `useCreateReservation` mutation hook that handles the asynchronous logic of creating a reservation, including loading states, error handling, and success callbacks. Upon successful reservation, a toast notification should be displayed to the user.

The `BookingPage.tsx` is the main entry point for customers to make reservations. It uses the `Layout` component from `@/components/Layout` to provide consistent navigation and footer. The page renders a `ReservationForm` component, passing the `useCreateReservation` mutation hook's `mutate` function and `isLoading` state as props. The page's content should be structured with a hero section at the top, followed by a section containing the reservation form. The hero section should feature a large, high-fidelity image relevant to a restaurant, a headline "Experience the Grandeur of Farmaaish" and a subheadline "Reserve Your Table for an Unforgettable Mughlai Feast."

The `ReservationForm.tsx` component is a controlled form that allows users to input their `customerName`, `customerEmail`, `customerPhone`, `reservationTime` (date and time), `numberOfGuests`, and `specialRequests`. It uses local state to manage form inputs and validates them before submission. Upon submission, it calls the `createReservation` function passed via props. The form should include input fields for all required reservation details and a submit button. Date and time selection should be user-friendly, perhaps using a date picker library. The form should display loading states and error messages appropriately. All monetary values (if any were to be displayed here, which there are none for reservations) would be formatted using `toLocaleString('en-IN', { style: 'currency', currency: 'INR' })`.

**Interaction Flow:**
1. A user navigates to the `/book` route, which renders `BookingPage.tsx`.
2. `BookingPage.tsx` renders the `ReservationForm.tsx` component.
3. The user fills out the `ReservationForm` with their details.
4. Upon submission, `ReservationForm` calls the `createReservation` function provided by `BookingPage`.
5. `BookingPage`'s `createReservation` handler (from `useCreateReservation` hook) calls `reservationService.createReservation`.
6. `reservationService.createReservation` makes a POST request to `/api/v1/reservations` on the backend `reservation-system`.
7. The backend processes the reservation and returns a `ReservationResponse`.
8. The `useCreateReservation` hook's `onSuccess` callback is triggered, displaying a success toast and potentially redirecting the user or clearing the form.

== FEATURE INSTRUCTION (holistic brief for all files in this feature — use for context and inter-file contracts) ==
The Order Management feature handles the complete lifecycle of a customer's food order, from creation and payment processing to status updates and retrieval. It integrates with the `menu-management` feature to validate menu items and with a pre-scaffolded payment service for transaction processing. This feature provides both customer-facing and admin-facing APIs.

## Data Models

`Order.java` represents the main order entity, containing details like customer ID, total amount, delivery address, and current status. It has a one-to-many relationship with `OrderItem.java`.

`OrderItem.java` represents a single item within an order, linking to a `MenuItem` from the `menu-management` feature and storing the quantity and price at the time of order.

`OrderStatus.java` is an enum defining the possible states of an order (e.g., PENDING, CONFIRMED, OUT_FOR_DELIVERY, DELIVERED).

## Repositories

`OrderRepository.java` provides standard CRUD operations for `Order` entities. `OrderItemRepository.java` provides standard CRUD operations for `OrderItem` entities.

## Service Layer

`OrderService.java` encapsulates the core business logic:

### `createOrder(CreateOrderRequest request, UUID customerId): OrderResponse`
1. Validates the `CreateOrderRequest` to ensure all required fields are present and valid.
2. Iterates through `OrderItemRequest` objects in the request.
3. For each `OrderItemRequest`, it calls `menu-management`'s `MenuService.getMenuItemById(UUID id)` to retrieve the `MenuItemDto` and verify its existence and current price. If a menu item is not found, it throws a `ResourceNotFoundException`.
4. Calculates the total amount of the order based on the current prices of menu items.
5. Creates a new `Order` entity with status `PENDING` and saves it using `OrderRepository.save()`.
6. Creates `OrderItem` entities for each item in the request, linking them to the newly created `Order`, and saves them using `OrderItemRepository.save()`.
7. Calls the pre-scaffolded `PaymentService.createOrder(new CreatePaymentRequest(amount, "INR", "order_" + order.getId()))` to initiate a payment. If the payment fails, it throws an `OrderProcessingException`.
8. Updates the `Order` status to `CONFIRMED` if payment is successful and saves the updated order.
9. Returns an `OrderResponse` containing the details of the created order.

### `getAllOrders(): List<OrderResponse>`
1. Retrieves all orders from `OrderRepository`.
2. Maps `Order` entities to `OrderResponse` DTOs.
3. Returns the list of `OrderResponse` objects.

### `getOrdersByCustomerId(UUID customerId): List<OrderResponse>`
1. Retrieves orders for a specific customer from `OrderRepository`.
2. Maps `Order` entities to `OrderResponse` DTOs.
3. Returns the list of `OrderResponse` objects.

### `getOrderById(UUID orderId): OrderResponse`
1. Retrieves an order by its ID from `OrderRepository`.
2. Throws `ResourceNotFoundException` if the order is not found.
3. Maps the `Order` entity to an `OrderResponse` DTO.
4. Returns the `OrderResponse`.

### `updateOrderStatus(UUID orderId, UpdateOrderStatusRequest request): OrderResponse`
1. Retrieves the order by `orderId` from `OrderRepository`.
2. Throws `ResourceNotFoundException` if the order is not found.
3. Updates the order's status to the `newStatus` provided in the `UpdateOrderStatusRequest`.
4. Saves the updated order using `OrderRepository.save()`.
5. Returns the updated `OrderResponse`.

## Controllers

`OrderController.java` exposes public-facing APIs for customers:
- `POST /api/v1/orders`: Allows authenticated customers to place new orders. It consumes `CreateOrderRequest` and returns `OrderResponse`. Requires authentication.
- `GET /api/v1/orders/my-orders`: Allows authenticated customers to view their own orders. Returns a `List<OrderResponse>`. Requires authentication.
- `GET /api/v1/orders/{orderId}`: Allows authenticated customers to view a specific order by ID. Returns `OrderResponse`. Requires authentication.

`AdminOrderController.java` exposes admin-only APIs:
- `GET /api/v1/admin/orders`: Allows administrators to view all orders. Returns a `List<OrderResponse>`. Requires admin role.
- `GET /api/v1/admin/orders/{orderId}`: Allows administrators to view a specific order by ID. Returns `OrderResponse`. Requires admin role.
- `PUT /api/v1/admin/orders/{orderId}/status`: Allows administrators to update the status of an order. It consumes `UpdateOrderStatusRequest` and returns `OrderResponse`. Requires admin role.

## DTOs

`CreateOrderRequest.java`: Used for creating new orders. Contains `customerId` and a list of `OrderItemRequest`.

`OrderItemRequest.java`: Represents a single item within `CreateOrderRequest`, containing `menuItemId` and `quantity`.

`OrderResponse.java`: Used for returning order details in API responses. Contains order ID, customer ID, total amount, status, and a list of `OrderItemResponse`.

`UpdateOrderStatusRequest.java`: Used by administrators to change an order's status.

## Exception Handling

`OrderProcessingException.java` is a custom exception thrown for errors during order creation or payment processing.

== FEATURE INSTRUCTION (holistic brief for all files in this feature — use for context and inter-file contracts) ==
The Order Management feature handles the complete lifecycle of a customer's food order, from creation and payment processing to status updates and retrieval. It integrates with the `menu-management` feature to validate menu items and with a pre-scaffolded payment service for transaction processing. This feature provides both customer-facing and admin-facing APIs.

## Data Models

`Order.java` represents the main order entity, containing details like customer ID, total amount, delivery address, and current status. It has a one-to-many relationship with `OrderItem.java`.

`OrderItem.java` represents a single item within an order, linking to a `MenuItem` from the `menu-management` feature and storing the quantity and price at the time of order.

`OrderStatus.java` is an enum defining the possible states of an order (e.g., PENDING, CONFIRMED, OUT_FOR_DELIVERY, DELIVERED).

## Repositories

`OrderRepository.java` provides standard CRUD operations for `Order` entities. `OrderItemRepository.java` provides standard CRUD operations for `OrderItem` entities.

## Service Layer

`OrderService.java` encapsulates the core business logic:

### `createOrder(CreateOrderRequest request, UUID customerId): OrderResponse`
1. Validates the `CreateOrderRequest` to ensure all required fields are present and valid.
2. Iterates through `OrderItemRequest` objects in the request.
3. For each `OrderItemRequest`, it calls `menu-management`'s `MenuService.getMenuItemById(UUID id)` to retrieve the `MenuItemDto` and verify its existence and current price. If a menu item is not found, it throws a `ResourceNotFoundException`.
4. Calculates the total amount of the order based on the current prices of menu items.
5. Creates a new `Order` entity with status `PENDING` and saves it using `OrderRepository.save()`.
6. Creates `OrderItem` entities for each item in the request, linking them to the newly created `Order`, and saves them using `OrderItemRepository.save()`.
7. Calls the pre-scaffolded `PaymentService.createOrder(new CreatePaymentRequest(amount, "INR", "order_" + order.getId()))` to initiate a payment. If the payment fails, it throws an `OrderProcessingException`.
8. Updates the `Order` status to `CONFIRMED` if payment is successful and saves the updated order.
9. Returns an `OrderResponse` containing the details of the created order.

### `getAllOrders(): List<OrderResponse>`
1. Retrieves all orders from `OrderRepository`.
2. Maps `Order` entities to `OrderResponse` DTOs.
3. Returns the list of `OrderResponse` objects.

### `getOrdersByCustomerId(UUID customerId): List<OrderResponse>`
1. Retrieves orders for a specific customer from `OrderRepository`.
2. Maps `Order` entities to `OrderResponse` DTOs.
3. Returns the list of `OrderResponse` objects.

### `getOrderById(UUID orderId): OrderResponse`
1. Retrieves an order by its ID from `OrderRepository`.
2. Throws `ResourceNotFoundException` if the order is not found.
3. Maps the `Order` entity to an `OrderResponse` DTO.
4. Returns the `OrderResponse`.

### `updateOrderStatus(UUID orderId, UpdateOrderStatusRequest request): OrderResponse`
1. Retrieves the order by `orderId` from `OrderRepository`.
2. Throws `ResourceNotFoundException` if the order is not found.
3. Updates the order's status to the `newStatus` provided in the `UpdateOrderStatusRequest`.
4. Saves the updated order using `OrderRepository.save()`.
5. Returns the updated `OrderResponse`.

## Controllers

`OrderController.java` exposes public-facing APIs for customers:
- `POST /api/v1/orders`: Allows authenticated customers to place new orders. It consumes `CreateOrderRequest` and returns `OrderResponse`. Requires authentication.
- `GET /api/v1/orders/my-orders`: Allows authenticated customers to view their own orders. Returns a `List<OrderResponse>`. Requires authentication.
- `GET /api/v1/orders/{orderId}`: Allows authenticated customers to view a specific order by ID. Returns `OrderResponse`. Requires authentication.

`AdminOrderController.java` exposes admin-only APIs:
- `GET /api/v1/admin/orders`: Allows administrators to view all orders. Returns a `List<OrderResponse>`. Requires admin role.
- `GET /api/v1/admin/orders/{orderId}`: Allows administrators to view a specific order by ID. Returns `OrderResponse`. Requires admin role.
- `PUT /api/v1/admin/orders/{orderId}/status`: Allows administrators to update the status of an order. It consumes `UpdateOrderStatusRequest` and returns `OrderResponse`. Requires admin role.

## DTOs

`CreateOrderRequest.java`: Used for creating new orders. Contains `customerId` and a list of `OrderItemRequest`.

`OrderItemRequest.java`: Represents a single item within `CreateOrderRequest`, containing `menuItemId` and `quantity`.

`OrderResponse.java`: Used for returning order details in API responses. Contains order ID, customer ID, total amount, status, and a list of `OrderItemResponse`.

`UpdateOrderStatusRequest.java`: Used by administrators to change an order's status.

## Exception Handling

`OrderProcessingException.java` is a custom exception thrown for errors during order creation or payment processing.
